tests.question: Can a preregistered jet-base model without a shadow-like central depression explain the calibrated visibility amplitudes and closure quantities as well as the ring-like model family?
tests.observable: Out-of-sample visibility and closure-quantity predictive performance of jet-only and ring-capable model families.
tests.method: Fit preregistered jet-only and ring-capable forward models to a training subset; compare predictions on held-out baselines, times, or frequency channels using a reviewed model-comparison rule.
tests.support_condition: Jet-only models match or outperform ring-capable models on held-out observables without introducing an equivalent central depression.
tests.refutation_condition: Jet-only models fail reviewed held-out data-consistency thresholds while ring-capable models pass.
tests.inconclusive_condition: Model families have unequal flexibility, held-out data are not independent, or calibration uncertainty dominates the comparison.

tests.question: Does one jet-only physical model simultaneously explain horizon-scale millimeter structure and independently observed jet behavior?
tests.observable: Joint predictive consistency across EHT-scale observables and independently measured larger-scale or multiwavelength jet constraints.
tests.method: Register a joint physical model and predict observables not used in fitting, including orientation, polarization, spectrum, or time variability where available.
tests.support_condition: A jet-only model makes successful independent predictions across scales without requiring shadow-like structure.
tests.refutation_condition: Jet-only models that fit one scale systematically fail preregistered independent observables while ring-capable models remain consistent.
tests.inconclusive_condition: The joint model is tuned after observing test data or cross-instrument uncertainties are not comparable.

independence_requirements: At least one test dataset must not be used for model fitting.
Model flexibility and parameter counts must be accounted for.
Multiwavelength observations must have independent instrument provenance.
Prediction targets and acceptance rules must be registered before evaluation.
limitations: Failure of a particular jet-only family does not refute every conceivable jet-dominated explanation.
Successful ring-capable models do not uniquely identify a Kerr geometry.
